idea-plugin.name: AI Relay
idea-plugin.description:
AI Relay — your Gemini on Vertex or Apigee, as a coding agent and in GitHub Copilot

A chat panel with coding agents that work over the whole project: Gemini through an Apigee gateway, Vertex AI or the Gemini API, and Microsoft 365 Copilot through your own signed-in web session. As a bonus, Claude through the Claude Code CLI if you have it.

The same Gemini connection can also be a model inside GitHub Copilot: the airelay serve command runs a local model server Copilot connects to as a Custom Endpoint.

Highlights

  • Agents, not autocomplete — they read, search, edit and run commands across the project
  • Streaming transcript with live tool activity and expandable output
  • Permissions — confirm each tool, accept edits automatically, or let it run
  • Editor-aware — include the current selection with one checkbox
  • Web access and Maven Central lookups so answers about versions are checked, not guessed
  • MCP servers in the same mcpServers file shape as Claude Desktop
  • Nothing to install — the agent runtime is bundled and runs on the IDE's own Java

This is the IDE front-end of the AI Relay command-line tool; the two share their configuration in ~/.airelay.

☕ Free and open source (MIT). Source, issues, and contributions: github.com/Chelayel/ai-relay.

Independent and unofficial — not affiliated with Anthropic, Google or Microsoft.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.5.1 — airelay serve logs every request it refuses and why — no key sent, a wrong key (only its first four characters), a key in an unexpected header, a page or host it does not serve — with the client that sent it, so a client that only says "invalid credentials" can be diagnosed from ~/.airelay/serve.log. A lowercase "bearer" is accepted.

2.5.0 — The agent explores the project the way Copilot's does: a new findFiles tool finds files by name or glob, Gemini is given the working directory and a map of the project, and it is told to read the files a question involves (callers, implementations, tests, config) instead of answering from the one file you are looking at. The file in the editor is now passed as a starting point to read from.

2.4.5 — airelay serve: the input limit it reports (banner, model list, VS Code model picker) is the context window less the output budget — 983,040 for Gemini, not 1,048,576 — because VS Code adds input and output and takes the sum as the window. The README shows the chatLanguageModels.json VS Code keeps for a Custom Endpoint.

2.4.4 — GitHub Copilot connects to airelay serve the same way in VS Code and JetBrains: Manage Models → Add Models → Custom Endpoint, with the values the server prints. The docs, the banner and the plugin description said JetBrains needed the Ollama option and --no-token; it does not. Ollama stays available for clients that offer nothing else.

2.4.3 — Gemini first: the agent menus, the setup and the descriptions now lead with Gemini (an Apigee gateway, Vertex or an API key) and its use as a model in GitHub Copilot, then Microsoft 365 Copilot; Claude Code stays available as a bonus, last in the agent dropdown. The README is short and starts with the GitHub Copilot setup; the details moved to the docs folder.

2.4.2 — airelay serve: --background works on Homebrew and the other packaged installs (it tried to run a java the packaged runtime does not have); addresses are shown as localhost, and the server listens on IPv6 too so clients that try ::1 first connect; airelay serve install is listed first, as the way to keep it running.

2.4.1 — airelay serve: a client that asks for a "deployment URL" works whether it uses the URL as given or appends /chat/completions itself, and Azure-style deployment paths take the model from the URL. It prints what Copilot's custom-model form asks for (deployment URL, API key, and per model its id, name, tool and vision support and token limits), runs in the background (airelay serve --background, status, stop) and can start at every login (airelay serve install, uninstall: launchd, systemd --user or the Startup folder). VS Code: an installed airelay older than the extension no longer wins over the newer CLI bundled in it, which is why the model dropdown showed one model for some; the panel says when the CLI in use is out of date.

2.4.0 — New: airelay serve — your Gemini connection (including an Apigee gateway) as a local model server for GitHub Copilot and other bring-your-own-model clients. In VS Code (1.104+) the AI Relay models appear in Copilot's model picker with nothing to configure; Copilot CLI and JetBrains (Ollama option) connect to it by URL. Copilot runs the agent, AI Relay forwards the model calls and keeps the credentials. See the README. In IntelliJ: run airelay serve --no-token and add it as Copilot's Ollama provider.

2.3.2 — The open file is attached reliably: Send attaches the file the chip shows, rather than looking up the active editor again (which often came back empty once the chat had focus). Clicking into the Output panel, a console, a diff or an image no longer clears it, and a chip clicked off comes back on for the next file.

2.3.1 — Opening a file from the chat (a diff header, a tool row, the MCP config) no longer uses an API IntelliJ 2026.3 deprecates.

2.3.0 — Gemini shows what each turn cost when you give it the rates (gemini.prices, USD per 1M tokens per model — e.g. an Apigee gateway's price list); the cost lands on the ✓ line under the turn, the session total in the header. The chat panel shows tool calls instead of hiding them under a collapsed line, names them as actions (Read, Edit, Run, Search, Fetch; an MCP tool as server · tool) and says what came back (3 lines, exit 0, the error). The per-round token line and the repeated MCP notice are gone from the transcript.

2.2.2 — Gemini through Apigee: the model picker lists only the models the gateway publishes, without the default model added next to them. Other connections: Gemini 4 Argon and 3.8 Flash are in the picker, and 3.8 Flash is the new default (3.7 Flash is deprecated). A Gemini turn ends as soon as the answer is complete, instead of staying busy until the connection closes (a gateway could hold it open for minutes).

2.2.1 — Gemini through Apigee: the model picker lists every model the gateway publishes (the Apigee models setting), not just the default one.

2.2.0 — Read-only mode: pick Read only in the mode menu (or type /mode search) and the agent reads and searches the code to answer, but never edits a file or runs a command. Copilot in the browser: a reply that is still rendering is waited for instead of being reported as missing, and a retried send keeps the conversation (it used to open a new chat that had lost the project context).

2.1.2 — An MCP server that exits at startup now fails at once with its own error message, not after a minute or with only an exit code. A server's own requests (such as a ping) are no longer mistaken for replies, and a server that dies right after connecting is restarted on the next call.

2.1.1 — "Apply to file" writes only inside the project; conversations are titled by what you typed, not by "Current file: …"; a Revert after Stop shows its diff; module roots on Windows are no longer all passed as extra directories; a link with a quote in it can no longer inject markup; a second message typed during a turn is added to the queued one instead of replacing it. In the CLI: one slow MCP call no longer wedges that server for the session; a shared Copilot browser is reconnected, never launched twice, and closed when its last user exits; a search cannot follow a symlink out of the workspace; a search provider's key never appears in an error; Ctrl-C leaves a wizard.

2.1.0 — A round of bug fixes: Stop stops the turn even with a draft in the box; a diff replayed from an earlier session no longer offers a Revert it cannot do; links in the transcript open in the browser again; Windows paths with a drive letter open in the editor; a restarted agent no longer leaves the panel stuck on "busy". In the CLI: Gemini no longer rejects the whole conversation after an interrupted tool round, a hung command is killed at its timeout, and two projects sharing one Copilot browser each get their own tab.

2.0.2 — The panel redraws at the right size after a monitor with another resolution is plugged in or unplugged; it used to stay small in one corner.

2.0.1 — Enter clears the composer again; a message sent while the agent was starting came back in the box.

2.0.0 — Smaller Gemini requests on long jobs; one shared browser for Copilot across projects; after 30 idle minutes the agent releases its Claude process, browser and MCP servers until the next message; a leaner JVM.

1.9.1 — The editor context names a file the agent can open, including files in modules outside the project directory. From this release the plugin and the extension ship at the CLI's version.

1.9.0 — Copilot is no longer given a system prompt; copilot.system.prompt adds one.

1.8.7 — Bundles the CLI at its release version; 1.8.6 bundled it labelled 1.8.3.

1.8.6 — The CLI version shows in the header tooltip and when the health dot is clicked.

1.8.5 — The connection line in the header wraps instead of being cut off. Several Gemini models, comma-separated in the settings, all appear in the model picker (Apigee).

1.8.4 — Closing the settings dialog with changed connection settings (an Apigee credential, a Copilot capture) restarts the agent on them; New is no longer needed.

1.8.3 — Version kept in step with the CLI, whose Windows console output is now readable; no plugin changes.

1.8.2 — Version kept in step with the CLI and the VS Code extension; no plugin changes.

1.8.1 — Gemini is the default agent. A change of agent or mode from the panel is saved at once, and the panel follows a change made on the settings page.

1.8.0 — The agent picker is a dropdown again, beside the model picker. On an Apigee gateway the model picker offers only the configured model.

1.7.0 — Slash commands, @file and #skill autocomplete in the composer; queued messages and draft memory; grouped tool calls; open-at-line from diffs and tool rows; Copy and Apply on code fences; permission prompts show the command or edit; a coloured agent switch with a health dot; history search; a setup card for an unconfigured agent; light-theme accents.

1.6.0 — Edits shown as diffs with Revert; earlier conversations listed and resumable; a model picker and, for Claude, a context and cost meter; agent personas from .claude/agents; the mode dropdown no longer restarts the conversation; a clock on the running tool and a summary line per turn.

1.5.0 — Drop files onto the panel or paste an image into the message box: images go to Gemini and Claude as pictures, text files go in with their contents, project-tree drags attach by path.

1.4.0 — A + menu in the composer: attach files, attach a skill (SKILL.md files in .claude/skills and friends), open the MCP config, settings. The panel is coloured by the agent in use, always shows the one actually running, and uses the IDE font. The demo backend is gone from the picker.

1.3.0 — The header shows the workspace folders and the configured MCP servers; the context chip keeps the file name whole and resolves paths against every content root.

1.2.0 — Live editor context: the chip under the message box follows the current file and selection and is attached automatically; click it to leave it out.

1.0.0 — First release: Claude, Gemini and Copilot in one tool window, settings form for every connection, live tool activity, permission prompts, editor selection as context.
